📍 OTHERS

YES BANK: Reports that reinstatement of AT1 bonds may involve a one-time ₹5,400–5,500 Cr accounting impact, with the bank examining its discretion regarding coupon payments following the Supreme Court judgment.

VIPUL: Reports standalone net loss of ₹14.17 Cr for Q1 FY27, with auditors issuing a qualified conclusion and highlighting concerns over project accounting, recoverability of loans and advances, and unprovided interest expenses.

BALKRISHNA PAPER: NCLT Mumbai admits capital reduction petition proposing adjustment of accumulated losses, reduction of equity face value from ₹10 to Re 1 without shareholder cash payment and reduction of ₹110 Cr preference share capital, with consideration deferred until adequate funds are available.

MANGALAM DRUGS: Discloses defaults totalling ₹15.57 Cr on cash-credit facilities with Bank of Maharashtra and Bank of Baroda, with overdue amounts outstanding for more than a year.

SYSCHEM (INDIA): Pays ₹1.25 Cr to Lotus Builders in full and final settlement of a dispute and plans to seek withdrawal or disposal of the pending NCLT matter.

A-ONE STEELS: Settles an NCLT matter for ₹3.8 Cr, paying the first ₹1.90 Cr instalment and scheduling the balance for payment by the end of October 2026.

SAL STEEL: Approves postal ballot seeking shareholder ratification of related-party transactions, including a ₹228.67 Cr unsecured short-term loan facility and other transactions with group entities.

SKIL INFRA: Adjourns its 14th Committee of Creditors meeting to October 21, 2026, as part of the ongoing corporate insolvency resolution process.

SGFINSERVE: Approves a 24.5% stake acquisition in SG Enterprise Solutions for approximately ₹1.23 lakh, intended to establish a centralised shared-services company for the group.

YES BANK: Supreme Court dismisses appeals filed by the bank, RBI and the Union of India against the setting aside of the March 2020 AT1 bond write-down.

🗞 BEAT THE STREET BULLETIN 🗞
Date: 16 October 2026
Telegram: https://t.me/BeatTheStreetnews

📍 ORDER WIN

DSSL: Wins ₹137.15 Cr order from Supreme Court of India for supply, installation and support of 728 servers across 728 district courts nationwide.

BL KASHYAP: Secures ₹200.02 Cr civil and structural works order from Nourish Developers for a commercial building at One DXP, Gurugram.

MAGELLANIC CLOUD: Wins ₹29.13 Cr railway CCTV surveillance order from Northern Railway's Moradabad Division for Kumbh Mela 2027, with execution within three months and a five-year AMC.

MONARCH: Wins ₹51.20 Cr Southern Railway order for traffic surveys, final location surveys and DPR submissions for new railway lines and track expansion projects.

PANCHMAHAL STEEL: Receives ₹25.25 Cr BHEL purchase order for supply of stainless steel wires to its Ranipet facility.

NEWGEN SOFTWARE: Wins ₹20.51 Cr international order through its UK subsidiary for enterprise content management, cloud hosting, implementation and support services over 3.5 years.

RDB INFRASTRUCTURE: Wins ₹20 Cr turnkey construction order from Oswal Residential Building for an experience centre in Kolkata.

DHABRIYA POLYWOOD: Secures ₹11.79 Cr order from Conscient Group for supply and installation of uPVC doors and windows, to be executed over 24 months.

SIYARAM RECYCLING: Wins ₹4 Cr export order from Dubai-based Green Metals FZCO for brass billets, with execution scheduled within 15 days.

ITCONS: Wins ₹67.42 lakh Indian Army contract for manpower outsourcing services for one year.

📍 ACQUISITION

REGENCY FINCORP: Approves ₹312.15 Cr preferential equity and warrant issue to fund acquisitions of a digital lending platform and gold loan business, alongside MSME lending expansion.

PERSISTENT SYSTEMS: Approves debt issuances of up to ₹8,000 Cr in NCDs and ₹1,000 Cr in commercial paper as part of financing for its Nagarro SE acquisition.

SGFINSERVE: Approves acquisition of a 15.5% stake in Succesship Technologies for ₹4.65 Cr to strengthen AI and digital lending capabilities, and a 24.5% stake in SG Enterprise Solutions for approximately ₹1.23 lakh.

📍 COLLABORATION

NOVATEOR RESEARCH LABORATORIES: Signs an exclusive three-year supply agreement with Pidilite Industries to develop, manufacture and supply enzyme-based aligner-cleaning foam and tooth-brightening strips, with revenue dependent on purchase orders.

LEMON TREE HOTELS: Signs an MoU with Omaxe to operate approximately 4,000 hotel keys across 10 projects, expanding its development pipeline to nearly 16,000 keys under an asset-light model.

OMAXE: Partners with Lemon Tree Hotels for 10 hotel projects comprising 4,000 keys, involving estimated investment of ₹4,000 Cr as part of its ₹6,200 Cr hospitality expansion.

DEE DEVELOPMENT ENGINEERS (DEEDEV): Signs a framework agreement with a domestic EPC contractor to jointly pursue nuclear power projects across PHWR, LWR and SMR technologies; the agreement carries no committed order value.

📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

AXIS BANK: Appoints Ananth Narayan G. as Additional Independent Director for four years from October 19, 2026, subject to shareholder approval.

FEDERAL BANK: Appoints Rajesh Varrier as Additional Independent Director for three years, effective October 16, 2026, subject to shareholder approval.

DATAMATICS: Appoints Dr Rajesh Gharpure as President and COO to oversee digital technologies, operations, AI consulting and other key functions.

E2E NETWORKS: Onboards Anandamoy Roychowdhary, Managing Director at Crane Venture Partners and former Sequoia Capital executive, as Strategic Advisor for AI and deep-tech strategy.

REMSONS INDUSTRIES: Appoints promoter Shivani Kejriwal as Additional Whole-Time Director for a five-year term from October 16, 2026, subject to shareholder approval.

BAJAJ CONSUMER CARE: Appoints Jitendra Mahajan as Non-Executive Independent Director, effective October 14, 2026; he brings over three decades of FMCG experience.

WILLIAMSON FINANCIAL: Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Anushree Biswas Dutt resigns for personal reasons, effective October 16, 2026.

📍 NEW PROJECTS

RAVINDRA ENERGY: Subsidiary Energy in Motion inaugurates an integrated electric commercial vehicle facility at Talegaon, Pune, backed by a planned ₹1,000 Cr investment and expected to generate over 2,000 direct and indirect jobs.

VRAJ IRON AND STEEL: Receives fresh environmental Terms of Reference for its greenfield steel plant, adding 32 MW of waste heat recovery power capacity, 28 MW of FBC power capacity and a phased bricks manufacturing unit.

THOMAS COOK INDIA: Subsidiary Sterling Holiday Resorts opens Sterling Vanyatara Tadoba, an 18-key wilderness resort in Maharashtra, expanding its wildlife hospitality portfolio and connecting its Pench, Tadoba and Tipeshwar properties.

UMIYA MOBILE: Opens 20 new retail stores across Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, expanding its presence across multiple cities.

📍 FUNDRAISING

SETL: Raises ₹71.48 Cr through preferential allotment of 24,39,750 equity shares at ₹293 per share to non-promoter investors.

REGENCY FINCORP: Board approves ₹312.15 Cr preferential fundraise through equity shares and convertible warrants at ₹50.50 per share, subject to shareholder approval.

SGFINSERVE: Approves investment of up to USD 5 million (approximately ₹48 Cr) to establish a wholly owned finance company in GIFT City, subject to regulatory approvals.

📍 CREDIT RATINGS

KPIL: CRISIL upgrades long-term rating to CRISIL AA+/Stable from CRISIL AA/Stable and reaffirms short-term rating at CRISIL A1+.

MEGAMONT: Infomerics assigns IVR BBB-/Stable and IVR A3 ratings to ₹18 Cr bank loan facilities of wholly owned subsidiary Mont International; the group reported FY26 revenue of approximately ₹2,705 Cr.

📍 FII STAKE CHANGES / BOUGHT-SOLD

MSCI / INDONESIA: MSCI considers downgrading Indonesia to standalone market status, citing market dysfunction concerns; feedback will be sought until April 2027, with a decision expected by June 2027.

📍 IPO

LANCER: Holds NSE listing ceremony on October 14, 2026, commemorating the listing of its equity shares on the exchange.

📍 Q2 / BUSINESS UPDATE

POPULAR VEHICLES: Q2 revenue rises 40% YoY, with vehicle sales up 51%; H1 FY27 revenue increases 46% as management cites festive demand, stronger bookings and network expansion.

L&T FINANCE: Q2 operating profit rises 32% YoY to ₹2,144 Cr, disbursements grow 27.15% to ₹24,027 Cr and AUM increases 27.6% to ₹1,36,635 Cr; NIM expands 34 bps QoQ to 8.88%.

FEDERAL BANK: Reports record quarterly profit, total business exceeding ₹6.4 lakh Cr and advances crossing ₹3 lakh Cr; NII grows 26%, fee income rises 32% and asset quality reaches decade-best levels.

ONWARD TECHNOLOGIES: Reports improved Q2 scale and profitability, adds 432 net employees during H1 FY27 and expects sustainable growth over the next three years, supported by AI-led transformation and digital engineering demand.

AURUM PROPTECH: Q2 total income rises 57% YoY to ₹137 Cr, adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 11.5% and the company reports its fourth consecutive quarter of positive PBT.

CROMPTON GREAVES CONSUMER: Reports a third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with 40 bps EBITDA margin expansion, 70 bps EBIT margin expansion and record quarterly export sales.

SOLARA ACTIVE PHARMA: Q2 revenue grows 33% to ₹417.8 Cr and EBITDA more than doubles to ₹76.9 Cr; ibuprofen business approaches breakeven, while strategic restructuring and future business plans are expected to be announced within 12 weeks.

L&T FINANCE, KABRA EXTRUSION, SBC EXPORTS, MANGALAM WORLDWIDE, SRI LOTUS, METRO BRANDS, ANGEL ONE, IIFL FINANCE AND TECH MAHINDRA: Included in the post-market Q2 results summary as companies reporting good results.

INDIAN BANK: Revises FY27 advances growth guidance to 13–14% and deposit growth guidance to 11–12%.

reports.text:
IRFC / RAILWAY SECTOR: Highlights the Railways' major capital expenditure plans, including dedicated freight corridors and eight announced high-speed rail projects, alongside an indicated ₹20 lakh Cr funding outlook over the next decade.

RELIANCE INDUSTRIES: Welcomes competition from Starlink in India's satellite communications market, reiterates that all players must comply with Indian laws and notes that Jio's satellite services are also awaiting regulatory clearances.

YES BANK: Supreme Court upholds the setting aside of the ₹8,415 Cr AT1 bond write-down; reinstatement could reduce CET1 ratio by approximately 250 bps, while the bank examines the judgment and evaluates legal options.

KARUR VYSYA BANK: Investec raises target price to ₹385 from ₹350 after strong quarterly performance, with PAT up 37% YoY to ₹790 Cr; management raises FY27 NIM guidance to above 4% and targets 18–20% loan growth.

IDBI BANK: Fairfax CEO describes IDBI Bank as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity in one of the world's fastest-growing economies.

NALCO / VEDANTA ALUMINIUM: Alcoa management expects further tightening in alumina markets outside China into Q4 and 2027; NALCO generates nearly one-third of its revenue from alumina.

SOLARA ACTIVE PHARMA: Management says its strategic review is at an advanced stage, with a shift towards higher-margin growth APIs, R&D and complex chemistry under consideration.

SHOPPERS STOP: Management says Q2 demand momentum remained strong following Q1, supported by festive-season traction, premiumisation and experiential retail, while targeting debt-free status by the end of Q3.

FEDERAL BANK: Management says it continues evaluating inorganic growth opportunities across core banking and other financial services, with nothing currently to disclose.

📍 USFDA / REGULATORY

ZIMLAB: Receives TGA GMP certification for its Kalmeshwar, Nagpur manufacturing facility, covering multiple non-sterile dosage forms and strengthening prospects for Australian and other international markets.

WANBURY: Receives nine USFDA “No DMF Deficiency” letters for Metformin HCl DMF and similar letters for Paroxetine and Diphenhydramine HCl; new Metformin businesses in Saudi Arabia and Mexico offer approximately ₹25 Cr annual revenue potential.

📍 CLARIFICATION

KISSHT: Clarifies that its ₹832.2 Cr preferential issue price is fixed at ₹314.11 per share, in line with the SEBI ICDR floor price and supporting valuation documentation.

ATUL: Clarifies reports concerning treated effluent discharge into the Par river, stating that the affected pipeline section was isolated, discharge voluntarily suspended pending repairs and released effluent complied with prescribed standards during the incident.

📍 LAUNCHES

AAYUSH WELLNESS: Launches calcium and vitamin tablets containing calcium citrate, vitamin D2, magnesium, zinc and folic acid, expanding its presence in the bone and joint health segment.

NUCLEUS SOFTWARE: Wins the CII National AI Award 2026 for its Generative AI Visual Report Agent, which converts loan statements into personalised narrated video summaries in over 10 Indian languages and Arabic.

📍 INCORPORATE / CORPORATE STRUCTURE

SHRIRAM FINANCE: Renames wholly owned subsidiary Shriram Overseas Investments Limited to Shriram Gilts Limited, effective October 15, 2026, following RBI approval related to commencing Primary Dealer business.

SHADOWFAX: Board approves incorporation of a new wholly owned subsidiary in logistics and other services, subject to MCA approval, and allots 49,098 ESOP shares.

EVEREST INDUSTRIES: Pays ₹112.93 Cr in call money to wholly owned subsidiary Everest Buildpro, converting 1,54,150 partly paid-up shares into fully paid-up shares while retaining 100% ownership.

📍 IT NEWS

NUCLEUS SOFTWARE: Its award-winning Visual Report Agent integrates with FinnOne Neo and uses generative AI to simplify complex loan statements, with estimated customer education cost savings of 10–15%.

E2E NETWORKS: Adds AI and deep-tech investment expertise through its appointment of Anandamoy Roychowdhary as Strategic Advisor.

ATUL : CLARIFIES ON TREATED EFFLUENT DISCHARGE FROM SITE

• Company says incorrect information and videos are being circulated about effluent discharge from Atul site into the Par river
• Uses an approximately 4-km long pipeline laid entirely within the estuary to discharge treated effluent into the estuarine zone
• New pipeline installation had been proactively initiated and is at an advanced stage, with necessary approvals obtained
• Accidental damage was identified in the existing pipeline about 1 km from the effluent treatment plant, within the estuary
• Effluent released during the short period complied with prescribed Gujarat Pollution Control Board standards
• Affected section isolated and discharge voluntarily suspended until repairs are completed and pipeline confirmed fit for safe operation
• Company does not expect any material impact due to this incident
Impact: Neutral (Company states no material impact; discharge through the affected pipeline remains suspended pending repairs)

reports.text:
Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

- Current Industry Data Pricing: Approximately ₹7.5 per GB
- 2016 Average Speed: 2.5 Mbps
- Current Industry Average Speed: 68 Mbps

FOUR FUTURE GROWTH ENGINES

1. MOBILITY
- Potential additions: 340 million customers over five years
- First-Time SIM Users: 100 million potential customers
- 2G-to-4G/5G Migration: 240 million subscribers
- Added three times more net active subscribers than its nearest competitor last financial year

2. HOME BROADBAND
- Existing Home Pass: Nearly 40 million homes
- Long-Term Target: 100 million connected homes
- India's Addressable Market: Approximately 300 million homes

- 40% of net additions come from outside Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities
- Jio claims 67.5% of India's net fixed broadband additions
- JioAirFiber supports areas where fibre deployment is difficult

3. ENTERPRISE & DIGITAL SERVICES
- Estimated Enterprise Opportunity: $56 billion
- India has approximately 350,000 leased lines
- Jio connects 65% of India's bank branches
- Target markets include BFSI, retail, hospitality and cybersecurity
- JioPC brings cloud computing to businesses through set-top boxes

4. GLOBAL TECHNOLOGY EXPORTS
- Plans to monetise its proprietary telecom technology stack
- Managed-service partnerships target international telecom operators
- Strategy aims to reduce partners' upfront infrastructure investment
- Long-term ambition includes software-led 6G deployment

PROPRIETARY TECHNOLOGY & AI
- Over 7,220 patents filed
- More than 12,000 Jio engineers
- Technology stack spans networks, home platforms, devices and applications
- Google Gemini partnership reportedly added 30 million subscribers for Gemini
- Planned Voice AI service includes transcription and call summaries

- AI applications target customers, network efficiency and digital services
- Jio aims to make future 6G upgrades more software-driven

HOME TECHNOLOGY INNOVATION

- Next generation targets 5 Gbps download and 1 Gbps upload

- Revenue three years earlier: Approximately ₹1,09,558 Cr

- Long-Term Thinking: Invest beyond short-term business cycles

- Financial Prudence: Maintain strong balance sheets

Cyient DLM Q2 FY27. Three numbers, three different stories.

Revenue ₹393 cr, up 26.5%. Order book ₹2,814 cr, all-time high, book-to-bill 1.6x. H1 revenue up 30%. That part is clean. 

Reported PAT ₹34 cr looks like +6%. Ignore it. ₹18 cr of that is an earnout reversal on the Altek deal, non-cash, same as last year’s Q2. Clean PAT is ₹15.8 cr, up 25.8%, tracking revenue. That’s the number.

Now the one that will trend: EBITDA margin 8.7%, lowest in six quarters. Why? Box build revenue up 86% YoY and now 37% of sales (more bought-out material per rupee), plus a fully loaded sales team and product development costs expensed, not capitalized.

Management says this is worth 150-200 bps of zero absorption today. Guide: 9-10% for FY27, double digit from FY28.

What the order book doesn’t show: a $1.5 bn bid pipeline at ~40% win rate, and ~$1 bn of 7-9 year B2S programs that only enter the book once design is done. Production FY29, ramp FY30. 🔭

So you’re paying today’s cost base for a revenue base two years out. Q3 margin is the test. Below 9% and the story needs re-underwriting.

1. Net worth
• Reported net worth stood at INR 510.62bn.
• Scenario A: INR 426.47bn, down 16.5%, with BVPS declining from INR 16.3 to ~INR 13.6.
• Scenario B: INR 372.92bn, down 27.0%, with BVPS declining to ~INR 11.9.

2. PAT
• Potential liability equals 2.4x / 4.0x FY26 PAT of INR 34.76bn under Scenarios A/B.
• If fully charged to P&L, FY26 would swing to a loss of ~INR 49.39bn / INR 102.94bn, respectively.

3. Loan growth
• Against FY26 net advances of INR 2,734.45bn, the liability amounts to 3.1% / 5.0% of the loan book under Scenarios A/B, respectively.

4. Capital adequacy
• Reported CET-1 / CRAR stood at 13.5% / 15.3%.
• Scenario A: CET-1 declines to ~10.9% (-257bps) and CRAR to ~12.7%.
• Scenario B: CET-1 declines to ~9.3% (-421bps) and CRAR to ~11.1%, below the 11.5% minimum CRAR requirement including CCB, potentially necessitating a capital raise.

5. If AT-1 bonds are reinstated
• Annual coupon outgo would be ~INR 7.72bn pre-tax and INR 5.87bn post-tax, equivalent to ~12.4% of FY27E PAT of INR 47.42bn.
• Reinstatement would restore AT-1 eligibility as Tier-1 capital, partly cushioning the capital adequacy impact.

*Valuation implications*
• At ~INR 18/share, the stock trades at ~1.1x reported FY26 P/BV.
• P/B rises to ~1.3x / 1.5x on adjusted book value under Scenarios A/B, respectively.

*Key monitorables*
• Settlement could involve cash payment, bond reinstatement or conversion into equity, with the latter potentially diluting shareholders.
• Past coupons remain uncertain given the non-cumulative and discretionary nature of AT-1 coupons. Principal-only repayment remains our base case.
• The accounting treatment (P&L versus reserves) will determine the reported earnings impact, although the net-worth hit remains.
• Settlement timelines, potential staggered payments and any review/curative petition remain key monitorables.

*Bottom line*
Under our base case, net worth could decline by 16.5%, with the liability equivalent to 2.4x FY26 PAT and CET-1 falling by ~257bps. The resulting capital hit could constrain lending capacity and delay RoE recovery. Clarity on the settlement mechanism and accounting treatment will be key. Currently, we have a sell rating on the stock.

MOSL on Fairfax IDBI Bank buy-in - 

- The CCEA has approved the sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52900 Cr (₹81/share), comprising 30.48% held by GoI and 30.24% by LIC.
- This is the biggest strategic disinvestment and will be the largest FDI in India’s financial sector to date
- GoI and LIC shall retain ~15% and ~19% stake, respectively, but will have no Board representation, which makes IDBI Bank a Promoter-led private bank. 
- Fairfax will have to make an open offer to minority shareholders after the share purchase agreement is signed. The terms aren’t public yet.
- Fairfax will have a five-year lock-in and a 15-year      glide path to bring its stake down to 26%. It should also merge or exit its ~40% stake in CSB Bank within two years.

We present below a snapshot of how the numbers for the merged entity will look should Fairfax decide to merge the two banks (IDBI Bank + CSB Bank)–

Balance sheet size: The balance sheet size shall increase by 13.1% with total assets increasing to INR5t.
Gold book mix post-merger: CSB’s Gold book mix is 54% of its overall book and stands at INR 219b. The acquisition shall lead to the Gold book increasing from 9% currently for IDBI to ~15% of the total merged entity loan book.
CD ratio: The C/D ratio post-acquisition for IDBI shall increase marginally to 80.6% from 79.5%, given CSB’s CD ratio is at 88.8% as on Jun-26.
Employee base: IDBI Bank has a higher employee base at 20,123 vs 8,187 for CSB Bank, taking the combined base to ~28,310.
Branch count: IDBI Bank has 2,243 branches vs 862 for CSB Bank, taking the combined network to ~3,105 branches.
CASA mix & Cost of Funds: IDBI Bank's CASA ratio is higher at 43.6% vs 19.4% for CSB Bank, resulting in a combined CASA of      ~40.7%. Cost of funds stands at 4.7% for IDBI vs 6.6% for CSB.
NIMs: IDBI Bank's NIM stands at 3.61% vs 3.66% for CSB Bank, implying a broadly neutral impact on the combined entity's NIM at ~3.6%. CSB's gold loan-heavy portfolio (54% of advances) supports yields.
Opex: IDBI Bank's C/I ratio is lower at 52.0% vs 64.6% for CSB Bank, with the combined ratio at ~54.6%, offering scope for operating efficiencies.
Credit costs & Asset quality: IDBI Bank's credit cost stood at -1.1% vs 0.5% for CSB Bank. GNPA/NNPA      stood at 2.3%/0.2% for IDBI and 1.8%/0.4% for CSB.
RoA/RoE: IDBI Bank reported RoA/RoE of 2.2%/14.6% in FY26 vs 1.2%/12.9% for CSB Bank.
BVPS and valuations: The BVPS of CSB is INR 289 as against INR 64.8 of IDBI. P/B on a trailing basis for both the entities stands at 1.1x and 1.4x currently.

MRPL has delivered a blockbuster Q2 but the numbers need some context.

Revenue rose 37% YoY to ₹35,590 Cr, while EBITDA more than doubled to ₹3,210 Cr. PAT surged 194% to ₹1,881 Cr.

The interesting part? Refinery throughput actually declined from 4.43 MMT to 4.18 MMT.

So, the earnings jump was not driven by higher volumes. Elevated crude and product prices lifted the reported topline, while the rising-price environment likely aided inventory valuation and refining profitability.

EBITDA margin consequently expanded from 6.0% to 9.0%.

However, MRPL has not separately disclosed its GRM or inventory gain in this release so the entire quarterly profit should not be treated as a steady-state run rate.

Other notable updates:

• H1 PAT reached ₹2,796 Cr versus ₹367 Cr last year
• ₹3 per share interim dividend announced
• First international credit rating of BBB- from Fitch
• Storage and distribution network expanded across Goa, Kochi, Mangaluru, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
• Bengaluru terminal secured certification for SAF blending with ATF
• New ONGC Group JV formed for petrochemical marketing

Strong quarter, undoubtedly but refining remains cyclical. The next results will reveal how much of this profitability came from sustainable operating margins and how much from the crude-price cycle.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now

*KEY TAKEAWAYS: CONCALL BY MR. RAAMDEO AGARWAL*
*Motilal Oswal Wealth Management | 10th Oct 2026*

*MARKET AT RARE VALUATION OPPORTUNITY - TIME TO DOUBLE UP, NOT SELL*

*1. Valuation is at multi-year low - 18% discount to average*
Nifty is currently trading at *17.2x 12-month forward P/E*, vs its 10-year average of *20.9x*. This is an *18% discount to Long Period Average*.
This is the same level we saw in COVID crash of 2020.
From the Sep'24 peak, valuations have cooled sharply:
*Nifty-50: 24.8x -> 17.2x (-31%)*
Midcap-150: 35.6x -> 22.8x (-36%)
Smallcap-250: 25.0x -> 23.2x (-7%)

*2. A unique situation in history*
For the *first time ever*, Indian Economy is doing well BUT Markets are at 52-week low and giving *negative returns in last 2 years*.
We remain the *Fastest Growing Economy, but the Worst Performing Stock Market* in the world. This gap will not last long.

*3. All headwinds are already priced in*
Market has already absorbed everything together:
Higher Crude Oil prices, Depreciating INR, Rising Bond Yields, Super El Nino.
Despite all this, our earnings engine is intact.

*4. Earnings have started to show - 20-25% growth expected*
Nifty 2Q earnings expected at *Sales +17% / PAT +27% YoY*.
MOFSL Universe PAT growth to hit an *11-quarter high of 22%*.
This is a broad-based recovery - for the first time in years, *almost every sector is expected to grow.*
Key contributors: *Cement (+35%), EMS (+34%), Retail (+22%), Consumer Durables (+20%)*
Auto volumes up >30%, Bank credit growth at decade high.
Markets are trading at *PEG < 1* - meaning you are paying less than earnings growth. Very attractive.

*5. Our Top Picks across Sectors*
*Large caps*
Reliance, LT, bharti, sbi, hdfcbank, kotak,tcs & infy,adaniports,adani power, adani enterprise
*Midcaps*
Trent,idea,Fluorochem,Cummins, ENRIN,GVTD, Kirloskar Oil, , Syrma SGS, MTAR, Divi Labs, Laurus Labs, Rubicon Research,  Shaily Engg, MolBio Diagnostics, Pearl Global, Welspun Living, Navin Fluorine,  Samvardhana Motherson, sonacoms,eternal, paytm,lenskart
*Small caps*
Aequs, marine, paragmilk,fredun pharma, one source, senoras pharma, samman capital, dynamatic technology,kwality walls,sasken technology,sudarshan chemical

*6. What can trigger the sharp reversal?*
US Bond Yield normally peaks at *5.3% to 5.5%* and appears to be in an overbought zone. Similarly, USDINR also looks to be peaking at these levels.
If there is any positive news on the war front and Crude cools off to *$60*, we will see a massive correction in Bond Yields and appreciation in INR.
That will be a powerful trigger for markets to re-rate sharply from these depressed valuations.

*CONCLUSION:*
In 2024, Nifty traded at 25 PE. Today it is at *31% discount* to that peak, while earnings have started to revive.
In worst of times, we get the best of opportunity.

This is not the time to sell in panic. *This is the time to double up investments and accumulate quality. Don't miss this opportunity.*

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.

Is India investing enough for future capacity

India is usually described as a consumption economy. Consumption contributes >60% of GDP. But the story becomes incomplete when we ignore what's happening on the investment side and other aspects of our economy

India's Gross Capital Formation is ~32.6% of GDP. Lower than China's ~40%, but China's per capita GDP is several times of India's. Comparing ratios without considering income levels misses the context.

A developing country cannot allocate every ₹ toward factories & infra. A large share of resources must also support the bottom of the pyramid through housing, healthcare, education & welfare.

A harmonious society requires a minimum standard of living for those at the bottom. India is building capacity while simultaneously funding social stability. That's a tougher balancing act than many realize.

So let's move beyond GDP narratives & look at hard physical data. India's share of global GDP is only ~3.5% yet produces roughly 10% of the world's steel. Steel almost 3x our weight in global GDP. Steel isn't consumed for consumption's sake, but goes into factories, rail tracks, power plants, ports, airports, infrastructure etc

Cement tells the same story. India produces ~400 MT annually out of ~4,000 MT globally. Again, roughly 10% global share despite only ~3.5% share of world GDP. Countries don't consume steel & cement at this scale unless they are building physical assets. These are the raw materials of future GDP.

Power generation presents a slightly different picture. India's share of global electricity output is lower than steel & cement, but still materially ahead of its global GDP share. India with 1800bn units vs 32,000bn units, 6% global share

The evidence suggests India is investing for future capability. One may argue the investment cycle started later than it should have, but the direction is unmistakable. Steel, Cement & Power share point toward economy preparing for a much larger future.

The scale of projects are also changing. DFCs, industrial corridors, semiconductor fabs, renewable energy parks, metros, airports, transmission corridors & logistics networks are larger than anything India attempted before.

If this trend continues, India's share of global steel, cement & power usage is likely to keep rising. Higher material intensity today is often a precursor to higher economic output tomorrow.

Maybe the better way to describe India isn't "consumption economy." It's a country simultaneously consuming, uplifting millions & building future productive capacity. 
India need a balancing act of Building future and taking care of the needy, which it is working towards

De-Dollarization lets peek into central bank reserves

Central banks are diversifying but US$ isn't giving up the throne anytime soon. Headlines scream de-dollarization bt US$ still makes up ~57% of global FX reserves. That's down from decades ago, but still miles ahead of everyone else.

Euro is the 2nd largest reserve currency at ~20%. But Europe faces weak growth, aging demographics, fiscal stress & fragmented politics. Hence no comfort for people looking to diversify away from US$

Then its China. Despite its economic size, RMB is only ~2% of global reserves & ~2% of global payments. Clear reflection of trust issues with the dragon. deep capital markets, convertibility & rule of law issues also there

They're moving into something with no issuer at all: Gold. Central banks themselves are now one of the biggest sources of gold demand globally, roughly buy ~30% of annual global mine production

Gold isn't rising only because investors are bullish. Significant chunk of global prodn is locked away by sovereign balance sheets. In 2026, central banks gold buying at slower pace vs 2025 due to 60% price rise.

Among the Major buyers were Poland, China, Brazil, India etc. 
Then there are few sellers too. Turkey has been among the largest sellers this year, reportedly selling ~83t YTD to support liquidity & FX/US$ needs.

That’s the problem. Though world want to move away from US$ in the long term but  issue in the medium term created due to lack of US$ in the country. 
Case in point Turkiye

Russia has also been a notable seller, reducing reserves by ~44t YTD as it seeks hard-currency liquidity. But Russia is also large producer of Gold

Gold is becoming a reserve diversification asset in a world where trust in fiat issuers is fragmenting.
BUT de-dollarization in reserves doesn't mean de-dollarization in trade.
That’s two very different thing

Global trade still run on the USD infrastructure. That network effect is incredibly hard to replace.
So its two-step process. Trade continues in USD.
But exporting nations convert a portion of their accumulated surplus reserves into gold, commodities, sovereign funds or other reserve assets.

The world may keep transacting in dollars while increasingly choosing not to store all its savings in dollars.

Conclusion:
Real story is different from "the end of the USD."
Reserve diversification is real.
Dollar replacement is not. Not in near future
